title: Install safety wire on nuts, bolts, and turnbuckles
subject: General
assumptions: FAA-H-8083-30B pages 7-77 to 7-80 are the governing handbook section for this task.
The tightness and lift tests are required evidence even though a single photograph cannot show them.
openQuestions: Which variant a photo belongs to must be supplied at capture time; acceptance criteria differ between the bolt and turnbuckle variants.
Wraps-per-inch is only measurable from a photo if a scale reference is in frame. Confirm whether students will be asked to include one.

steps.text: Thread the wire into the bolt.

checks.text: The wire is routed so that tension from the wrap pulls the bolt in the tightening direction.
Both strands leave the starting hole at roughly equal length.
The wires meet the bolt hole at approximately 90 degrees.

errors.text: Wire routed in the loosening direction.
Strands grossly unequal, leaving too little wire to finish the run.

checks.text: Twist density measures 6-8 wraps per inch.
Wraps are uniform and tight, with no visible slack between the fasteners.

errors.text: Fewer than 6 or more than 8 wraps per inch.
Over-twisting; the run is taut to the point of work-hardening the wire.
Visible slack in the span between fasteners.

checks.text: The pigtail shows defined wraps and is curled back toward the bolt head.
The curled end lies parallel to the surface and presents no sharp end.

errors.text: Cut end left straight and uncurled — a sharp/FOD hazard.
Pigtail left overly long or with undefined wraps.

checks.text: A spare wire cannot be slid between the bolt head and the wire wrapping around it (the tightness test).
The wire cannot be lifted over the bolt head.

errors.text: Safety is loose enough to admit a probe wire under the wrap.
Wire can ride up and off the bolt head.

steps.text: Thread the wire into the bolt.

checks.text: The wire is routed so that tension from the wrap pulls the bolt in the tightening direction.
Both strands leave the starting hole at roughly equal length.

errors.text: Wire routed in the loosening direction.

checks.text: The plier jaws are locked on the wire at the next fastener hole, so the twisted length matches the span.

errors.text: Twisted length does not match the span, leaving slack or over-tension.

checks.text: Twist density measures 6-8 wraps per inch.
Wraps are uniform, with no slack in the span.

errors.text: Fewer than 6 or more than 8 wraps per inch.
Pliers released under load, producing an abrupt change in twist pitch partway along the run.

checks.text: The pigtail shows defined wraps and is curled back toward the bolt head.
The curled end lies parallel to the surface and presents no sharp end.

errors.text: Cut end left straight and uncurled — a sharp/FOD hazard.
Tooling marks from the plier jaws on the finished wraps.

checks.text: A spare wire cannot be slid between the bolt head and the wire wrapping around it.
The wire cannot be lifted over the bolt head.

errors.text: Safety is loose enough to admit a probe wire under the wrap.

steps.text: Cut two pieces of safety wire.

checks.text: Two wires are used, each cut to approximately 30 inches.

errors.text: Only one wire used, or wire too short to complete both ends.

checks.text: Each wire is inserted through the turnbuckle barrel into two even strands, with the second wire mirroring the first in the opposite direction.
Strands lie streamlined along the barrel toward the cable ends.

errors.text: Strands not mirrored, leaving the turnbuckle secured in one direction only.
Wire stands proud of the barrel instead of lying streamlined.

steps.text: Perform the wraps on the ends of the wires.

checks.text: Exactly 4 tight wraps per wire at each end.
Wraps are tightly coiled with no gaps between turns.
No tooling marks on the finished wraps.

errors.text: Wrap count other than 4 per wire.
Loose or gapped coils.
Plier tooling marks scarring the wrap.

checks.text: The completed safety presents a streamlined silhouette against the turnbuckle.
4 wraps per wire, tightly coiled with no gaps.
Wire ends are curled so no sharp hazard remains.

errors.text: Sharp uncurled wire ends left exposed.
